title: Before its TGE a Prime is credited with only 70% of the income it generates
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.7.5 fixes both a start date and a split: "'Income Generation' shall be deemed to commence on July 1, 2025. From that date until the Prime's TGE, seventy percent (70%) of any income generated by the Prime's activities shall be credited to its capital account (net of any expenses paid by Sky...), subject to any penalties."

A.2.8.2.2.2.7.6 makes "Income" deliberately broad — Distribution Rewards, the 2025 bonus, "any Platform Fees charged to users," RWA origination and servicing fees, "and the blended cost of allocation spread between Junior and Senior Risk Capital" — covering revenue "received or accrued," so the split cannot be avoided by timing receipts.

The 30% Sky retains during the pre-TGE window is best read as the price of operating on Sky's capital and infrastructure before the Prime has stood up its own token, governance and balance sheet. It also creates a standing incentive to complete the TGE promptly, since the retained share ends when the Prime becomes independently capitalised.

Note the word "deemed." Income Generation begins on a stated calendar date regardless of when actual revenue started, which removes any argument about when a Prime's activities became income-generating — the same simplification instinct that appears throughout the settlement rules.

Stacking matters here. A pre-TGE Prime can face the 70% credit, the 30% Token Launch Penalty and the deduction of Sky-paid expenses simultaneously, all against the same income. The clauses are written to compose ("net of," "subject to any penalties") but the Atlas never states the combined effect, which is precisely the kind of interaction the deferred settlement mechanism will have to resolve.
description: Income Generation is deemed to start July 1 2025, and until the token event 70% of income is credited to the Prime's capital account net of Sky-paid expenses and subject to penalties.
